solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Something pub may serve fraud investigator

blocks.note: a scam is a fraud
PI is a private investigator

explanation.surface: A pub might offer the services of a fraud investigator, as if detectives were on the bar menu.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole opening phrase; 'fraud investigator' reads as one job but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded prawns in a basket are a classic British pub meal, so they are an example of something served there.

clue.text: Spooner’s heavy bird of prey in kerfuffle

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so his version swaps them here

blocks.note: heavy is fat; it takes the K sound from the next word
a kite is a bird of prey; it takes the F sound from the previous word

explanation.surface: Someone describes a large hawk caught up in a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the F and K sounds of the two words turns the heavy hawk into a squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerfuffle is a commotion or fuss, and a spiteful scrap between two people is one such noisy row.

clue.text: Lacklustre guy entering bank

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: to guy someone is to tease them, as is to rib them
a bank of earth is a mound

explanation.surface: A dull man walks into a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a noun for a man, but it is the verb meaning to mock, and 'bank' is a raised heap, not a lender.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dying or stagnant has lost all vigour, so it is lifeless and without spark.

clue.text: Settled soon astride horse of French revolutionary

indicators.note: a rider astride sits with legs either side, so one piece straddles another
a revolution turns things round, so the word is turned back to front

blocks.note: 'in a bit' means soon
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
de is French for 'of'; the clue's 'of French' asks for the French word for of

explanation.surface: A horse belonging to a French revolutionary has been tamed and settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of French' asks for the French word for 'of', which 'revolutionary' then turns round; horse as H for heroin is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A settled region is one that people live in and occupy, so the past participle matches.

clue.text: Humbug sweets

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for nonsense
second meaning: baked fruit puddings topped with scone dough, sweets being British for desserts

explanation.walkthrough: A humbug is also a British mint sweet, so the two words seem to describe one confection; in fact 'cobblers' is British slang for rubbish, and sweets here means desserts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both British slang for rubbish talk and the name of fruit puddings with a scone crust.

clue.text: Revenue for government head opposed to postponing a vote

indicators.note: to postpone is to put off till later, so a letter is taken from its early place and set down further on

blocks.note: a capital is the head of a column, or a head city
against means opposed to
taken as written, moved from the front of the previous piece
a cross marks a vote on a ballot

explanation.surface: A government chief opposes delaying a ballot, hoping for the revenue.
explanation.walkthrough: The A at the front of the 'opposed to' word is put off until after it, and the cross then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: This levy on profits from selling assets is collected by the state, making it a source of public income.

clue.text: Hold huge bra tight

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, and drunken letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice on keeping an oversized bra firmly fastened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' seems to describe the hold, but it is the drunk sense signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, crushing embrace is a kind of hold, as wrestlers use the word for a grip.

clue.text: One doing rough physical work, or fencer at work

indicators.note: letters at work are being operated on and moved about

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A labourer, or else a swordsman in action.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'or' looks like it offers two definitions, but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy who uses physical intimidation to make people comply, as for a gang or in ice hockey, does rough work.

clue.text: Big stories of bands holding record up

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece sits within another
in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top, turning the letters round

blocks.note: sashes are bands of cloth worn round the body
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Newspaper headlines about pop groups with a record climbing the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bands' suggests pop groups, but it means strips of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper splash is a sensational front-page report, so prominent headline stories are this.

clue.text: Enterprise perhaps plays a leading role with it

blocks.note: an actor who stars plays the lead
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A business venture takes the lead and stays fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enterprise' reads as a business, but it is the spacecraft from Star Trek, with 'perhaps' marking it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The USS Enterprise in Star Trek is a fictional interstellar spacecraft, an example of this vessel type.

clue.text: Visibly upset, losing face in rebuke

indicators.note: the face is the front, so losing it drops the opening letter

blocks.note: someone tearful is visibly upset

explanation.surface: Someone loses face and is visibly upset at being told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing face' sounds like embarrassment, but it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting a long angry scolding is informally called getting one of these, so it equals a reprimand.

clue.text: What you might see in a drill case, not all at once

definitions.text: What you might see in a drill case

blocks.clueFragment: What you might see in a drill case
blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: drill bits lying side by side in their box
second meaning: gradually, a little at a time

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical literal reading: the attachments for a drill sit next to one another in their case.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means gradually, in small stages, which is the opposite of doing everything simultaneously.

clue.text: Comedy’s opening with deity one’s seen in Greek play

indicators.note: an opening is where something begins, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: the initial letter of the word
Horus is the falcon-headed Egyptian god

explanation.surface: A comedy opens with a god appearing in a Greek drama, as with a deus ex machina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comedy' and 'Greek play' make the deity look Greek, but the god needed is Egyptian.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Greek drama featured a group of performers commenting on the action, so one is seen in every such play.

clue.text: Making clothing line is irritating

indicators.note: clothing something covers it all round, so one piece is wrapped in another

blocks.note: netting a sum is making it, as in earning a profit
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Producing a clothing range turns out to be annoying work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making clothing line' reads as fashion manufacture; 'clothing' is the verb meaning to wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle someone is to annoy them, as a stinging plant does, so the present participle means annoying.

clue.text: Accessory for man reluctant to have drink cold at first

blocks.note: to neck a drink is to gulp it down, British slang
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
loth is a spelling of loath, meaning reluctant

explanation.surface: A man unwilling to have a cold drink first needs some accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' places the drink and the cold before the reluctant piece rather than picking first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat or similar band of fabric tied around a man's throat is a fashion item he wears.

clue.text: Boss working hard to clear evidence of debts

indicators.note: to clear something is to remove it, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: a studious person works hard at their books
IOUs are written acknowledgements of money owed

explanation.surface: A boss works hard to pay off the company's debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager, but it is the raised knob on a shield or surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a decorative raised knob, and a large-headed ornamental nail or knob is the same thing.

clue.text: Funny sitcom about lives in an ancient school

indicators.note: something funny is peculiar or odd, so the letters are rearranged
about means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
'lives' as in exists, which is what 'is' means

explanation.surface: A comic television show is set in a school of the ancient world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' sits naturally beside 'sitcom' as praise but signals rearrangement; 'school' means a school of thought.
explanation.definitionFit: This Greek philosophy founded by Zeno at Athens is a classical school of thought, school meaning a movement.

clue.text: Can’t rude jockeys perform with some restraint?

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre for position, so the letters jostle into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A question whether badly behaved jockeys can ride with a bit of restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jockeys' looks like the riders, but it is a verb, and 'restraint' fits riders on a rein.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a part in a deliberately understated way, holding back emotion, is the meaning here.

clue.text: Love foreign bread you reportedly put away

indicators.note: what is reported is heard spoken, so a word gives its sound only
putting something away removes it from view, so letters are taken out

blocks.note: bread is slang for money, and euros are a foreign currency to a British setter
the letter name sounds like the pronoun

explanation.surface: A lover of foreign bread eats some up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' is slang for money, not a loaf, and 'put away' sounds like eating.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of desire personifies romantic passion, so the name stands for love itself.

clue.text: Unpackaged beds and one item of furniture that can be adjusted

indicators.note: unpackaged means stripped of its wrapping, so the outer letters go and the inner ones stay

blocks.note: the inner letters of the word
the Roman numeral for one
a table is furniture

explanation.surface: Flat-pack beds and an adjustable piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unpackaged' evokes flat-pack furniture, but it strips the outer letters off the word next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A text or file that is open to being revised or altered can be changed, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Nerd can do wrong, with daughter going great guns

indicators.note: doing something wrong puts it in a bad order, so the letters are rearranged
something going is leaving, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A geek can go astray, with his daughter getting on extremely well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going great guns' is an idiom for thriving, but 'going' removes a letter and 'great guns' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance is the collective term for heavy artillery and military weapons, so big cannons are this.

clue.text: A theologian welcomes lead Anglicans in Lent

indicators.note: a host welcomes guests inside, so one piece takes others in

blocks.note: taken as written
DD is Doctor of Divinity
the van is the leading part, as in vanguard
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A churchman welcomes senior Anglicans during the season of Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lent' sits at the end as if it were the church season, but it is the past tense of lend.
explanation.definitionFit: Money that has been lent has been handed over as a loan beforehand, which is to say paid in advance.

clue.text: Agony aunt periodically has outburst about paper

indicators.note: something done periodically happens at intervals, so every other letter is taken
about means around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: the first and third letters
a gush is a sudden outpouring
I is the Independent's short name, or its offshoot paper i

explanation.surface: A newspaper's agony aunt now and then explodes at her own paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agony aunt' looks like a single phrase, a newspaper advice columnist, but 'Agony' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe mental or physical suffering is anguish, a close synonym of extreme pain.

clue.text: One drug in prison in time for chilling?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
E is ecstasy
a cage is a prison

explanation.surface: A drug-taking inmate wonders whether prison is time to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chilling' is slang for relaxing, but here it means freezing, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A glacial period was an era when the planet grew very cold, a literal period of chill.

clue.text: Figure hosting company knocked back vermouth — it’s addictive stuff

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so one piece contains others
back means backwards, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: nine is a number, a figure
Co is the abbreviation for company
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A character in company downs a vermouth and finds it habit-forming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests drinking the vermouth; in gin and It, It means Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The alkaloid in tobacco is the substance that makes smoking habit-forming, so it is a dependency-causing chemical.

clue.text: Country wanting Yankee in charge, showing a certain inclination

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing

blocks.note: a European country
Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A country that wants an American in charge shows its political leanings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclination' reads as a political preference but means a slope, as in sloping type.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type leans to the right, so text set in it displays a particular slant.

clue.text: Steak sandwiches mostly capital for one in the orchestra

indicators.note: a sandwich holds a filling between its slices, so one piece goes inside another
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a T-bone is a cut of steak
Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: Steak sandwiches, mostly from the capital, feed a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like food beside 'steak' but is a verb for enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: This brass instrument with a slide is a standard member of the orchestra, so it is one of its players.

clue.text: Holder of a light fixture by area in theatre

blocks.note: a sports fixture is a match
a box is a private seating area in a theatre

explanation.surface: A lamp-holder for a light fitting placed beside a theatre area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light fixture' reads as one thing, a lamp; 'light' belongs to the definition and 'fixture' is a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A small container for matches holds the sticks used to strike fire, so it carries a means of lighting.

clue.text: Consider fixing frame of lattice repaired at last?

indicators.note: a frame is the edge of a thing, so only the outer letters are kept
fixing means attaching firmly around something, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: to heed is to take notice of, consider
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone considers mending a lattice frame that was finally repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is the shoemaker's foot-shaped block, so 'repaired at last' is a cobbler's job on a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe given a new heel has been mended on the cobbler's last, hence the question mark.
